neighbours.label: Fires on chemistry nouns for a prepared mixture of substances (solution, composition, solvents, mixture) when used about chemicals; quiet on 'solution' meaning an answer to a problem and on chemistry sentences without such a noun.
fire: The crystals were rinsed with a dilute saline solution before weighing.
Paint thinners and other organic solvents must be stored in metal cabinets.
The alloy composition was adjusted to raise the melting point.
The technician added the powder to a buffered aqueous solution.
Industrial degreasers often contain chlorinated solvents and surfactants.
The ceramic glaze composition includes silica, alumina and flux.
The precipitate was filtered from the acidic solution and dried.
Resin manufacturers blend each composition with a curing agent.
quiet: The managers were rinsed of doubt once a workable solution was found.
Paint brushes and other tools must be stored in metal cabinets.
The alloy was poured into molds to raise production volume.
The technician added the powder to a glass beaker on the bench.
Industrial kitchens often contain stainless counters and sinks.
The ceramic glaze was fired in a kiln for twelve hours.
The engineers offered a clever solution to the parking shortage.
Resin manufacturers ship each drum with a safety label.

predictions: 6/8 fire >= 0.3 (probes: aqueous solution 0.67, polymer composition 0.64, solvents 0.54); near misses mostly < 0.15 ('solution to the scheduling problem' 0.02); risk: chemistry context alone ('in a flask' 0.21).
notes: Probes (fraction of max 1.81): aqueous solution 0.67, polymer composition 0.64, cleaning solvents 0.54, acidic conditions 0.29, 'A mixture of' 0.31; non-chemical 'solution to the problem' 0.02; 'composition of the orchestra' 0.38 (so no composition near misses); chemistry without the noun 0.21.
